title: Thematic analysis in qualitative research: a step-by-step guide
summary: Thematic analysis finds patterns of meaning in qualitative data. Learn how to go from coded interviews to clear themes, with a worked example.
body_markdown:
What is thematic analysis in qualitative research? +


Thematic analysis works with most kinds of qualitative data, including interviews, focus group transcripts, and open-ended survey responses. Qualitative thematic analysis involves researchers coding qualitative data, then grouping related codes into themes that explain what participants mean in relation to the research questions.


How do you define thematic analysis? +


Braun and Clarke, who developed the most widely used version, give the thematic analysis definition as "a method for identifying, analyzing and reporting patterns (themes) within data."


What is reflexive thematic analysis? +


Reflexive thematic analysis is a form of thematic data analysis that recognizes the researcher's perspective and assumptions as part of how themes are developed. Researchers reflect on how their own interpretation shapes the coding and analysis, and treat themes as something they build from the data.


What is the difference between thematic analysis and content analysis? +


Thematic analysis interprets what participants mean, and content analysis counts how often something comes up. If several people in a meal delivery study mention late deliveries, content analysis records how many. Thematic analysis looks at what those comments say about the service, such as whether customers can plan meals around their orders.


How long does thematic analysis take? +


Timelines vary widely depending on how much data a team has and the tools it uses. When AI handles first-pass coding, researchers start from coded data and spend their time reviewing and refining the themes. In-house teams can then analyze more of their own studies.


Can AI do thematic analysis? +


AI can handle first-pass coding by tagging data excerpts and suggesting potential themes across large amounts of qualitative data. The researcher checks those codes against the data and makes the final call on how each theme is defined and what it can support, or if further analysis is needed.
